A Genuine Taste of Vietnam — Don't Miss This Gem!
Apr 2026 • Family
If you're visiting Ho Chi Minh City and want an authentic Vietnamese dining experience that leaves a lasting impression, Hoang's Kitchen is an absolute must. I had the pleasure of dining here recently and it exceeded every expectation.

The Vietnamese pancake (Bánh Xèo) was simply outstanding — crispy, golden, and perfectly filled, with that signature sizzle and lightness that's so hard to get right. It's the kind of dish that transports you straight into the heart of Vietnamese home cooking. Every bite felt crafted with care and love for the cuisine.

The other dishes we tried were equally impressive — fresh, vibrant flavours, beautifully presented, and generous in portion. What really stood out was how thoughtfully the menu caters to both traditional Vietnamese tastes and vegan diners — a rare balance that never felt like a compromise. The vegan options were full of flavour and creativity, not an afterthought.
The warmth and hospitality of the team made the whole experience even more special. It's the kind of place where you immediately feel welcome, and where the food speaks for itself.

I came as a visitor and left as a fan. If I'm ever back in Ho Chi Minh City — and I certainly hope to be — Hoang's Kitchen will be my first stop. Highly, highly recommended.

We were there for dinner at 8:15 today. The waiter informed us directly that the meal would take about 20 minutes – perfectly fine.

When the first dish arrived after almost 45 minutes, everything was still okay, although some specially ordered side dishes were already missing. About 10 minutes later, the waiter came back and suddenly told us that another ordered dish was no longer available and we should look at the menu again. By this time 60 minutes had passed since the order was placed.

We asked to bring at least the remaining dishes. After another 5 minutes the food came, but again something was missing, which we noticed again. Only 2–3 minutes later was this submitted.

Overall, the experience was unfortunately very disappointing. If you want to spend a nice and relaxing evening in a restaurant, this is the wrong place. The waiters seemed hectic throughout, which also transferred to the atmosphere.

The food itself was good, but everything else is unfortunately not recommended. We have not experienced anything like this during our entire trip to Vietnam – whether it is a simple restaurant or fine cuisine. There are definitely better addresses in Saigon.

The seafood bánh xèo was 3/5 — the fish sauce lacked depth, and while there was plenty of squid, it was very chewy and not sweet at all. Some of the carrot sticks served alongside tasted off—almost chemical, like gasoline, which was quite concerning.😰

The service was outstanding (5/5) — attentive and genuinely welcoming. The ambiance was lively, with many foreigners trying Vietnamese food. However, the restaurant was extremely dark, which is a major issue for me. Poor lighting can easily mask cleanliness problems, and unfortunately, that’s something I’ve seen used as a tactic before. It’s a big red flag in my book.
Overall, I gave it 3/5 mainly because of the excellent service, but I won’t be returning.

Food was so-so, the place really caters to tourists, so it lacks a bit of local authenticity. Taste is not bad, but I have tried other places in the area that are more delicious. 

My biggest disappointment was with service. Staff was initially friendly, but very “business-minded”. Friendliness of the person serving us dropped significantly when it came to the payment process and the tip was in his hand. He got annoyed because the first credit card did not work and it took a second attempt with another card. When he asked me to do a review on Google and I politely declined, he couldn’t get us out fast enough. 

My conclusion: A bit of a tourist trap… The restaurant is clever about playing the online algorithms - but there are much better choices around (for example, “Propaganda”, which is located on the other side of the palace. Both food and service were significantly better, and you see more locals there as well.

Highly recommend!!
Aug 2025 • Friends
I couldn’t recommend this restaurant enough, we very nearly walked past but I’m so glad we spotted it and ate here!! I got the Vietnamese chicken pancakes and fresh spring rolls. I was given a demonstration of how to cut and wrap my pancakes and they were so tasty and filling! My friend got the chicken and cashew rice stir fry and said the same about her meal. The food was so fresh and the service from walking in to leaving was faultless. The atmosphere was also great, it’s a busy restaurant but not too loud. I would highly recommend visiting here if you’re ever in Ho Chi Minh!

Ryan, who we assumed to be a supervisor, was very mindful of the condition and asked about all the ingredients they used to make sure it was safe for us. We had the summer rolls, beef with chilli and lemongrass and seafood fried rice - without soy sauce. The food was delicious, very fresh and refreshing flavours. The price is very reasonable, especially for the quality of service and meals. We highly recommend this restaurant. And if Ryan is serving you - well you got the jackpot!

main- Hanoi traditional fried fish &

Misleading menu
Feb 2025 • Couples
We decided to dine here on the basis of reviews we had read, and not bring far from our accommodation in HCM. The restaurant was busy when we arrived, service was sporadic, one of us received their drink and meal very quickly, whilst the other person was left with neither.
Food and drinks both finally arrived, but then we queried the fact that the side dish of seasonal vegetables for both our mains had not arrived. We were then told that the side dishes we were expecting were actually in the main dish? One of the dishes being a vegetable curry, listing carrot, potato and broccoli, there were no other vegetables included in the dish. The same with the chicken and lemongrass. Why are these listed on the menu as side dishes to accompany the main snd rice? Somewhat misleading. A shame as the food was reasonably tasty.
Service wasn't great, had to keep trying to get attention for further drinks and to look at desserts. Not sure either whether there was even any alcohol in the cocktail we ordered, if therewas it was certainlyminimal?
Sadly disappointed, we won't be trying them again whilst in HCM.
Would suggest that you check what you will actually receive with your meal when ordering, to save any disappointment.

Dec 2024 • Family
We came here for lunch on our first day in HCM City. The food was excellent and so was the service. Came back there for dinner for our last night in Vietnam, and were told to wait outside for 10 minutes until they could find a table, however they let the very next people walked up straight in. Turns out they had a bunch of free tables upstairs. But then the fun didn't stop there , despite having cocktails in the menu, they could not offer any, and then the spring rolls we ordered were sold out. Maybe goid for lunch when you are the only customers but expect to be disappointed for dinner.

Such a great experience and so fun to cook like a local and get to know both Miley and Quyet!
